summary: Only Hacker News was reachable today (Reddit, X, Bluesky, Stack Exchange and Mastodon were blocked), so this is a smaller, HN-only report. The strongest themes: a 1,000-point backlash against Postman's AI/telemetry behaviour, people still hand-typing expenses because bank syncing is unreliable, and a growing wish for search that filters AI slop.

ideas.title: Quiet API Client
ideas.oneLiner: A tiny, offline-only HTTP request tool with no account, no cloud sync and no AI, sold as a one-time purchase.
ideas.problem: A thread about Postman silently installing AI plugins and attempting to share API data hit 1,000+ points. Developers say they only want a 'glorified cURL GUI', but the popular tools push cloud accounts, AI features and pricing pages, so commenters expect every free option to be enshittified eventually.
ideas.targetUsers: Backend and mobile developers who poke at endpoints daily and handle secrets or internal APIs they cannot send to a vendor cloud.
ideas.monetization: One-time $19–29 license (no subscription) with a free tier; the 'no account, zero network calls' promise is the selling point. Optional team licence for shared collections via a git folder.
mvp: Send GET/POST/etc. requests with headers, query params, JSON and form bodies, and see a formatted response
Collections stored as plain files in a folder, so they can be committed to git
Environment variables with secrets kept in the OS keychain
Import from cURL, Postman and Insomnia exports
Verifiable zero-egress mode: no telemetry, works fully offline, with a documented network allowlist

competitors.name: Bruno
competitors.gap: Named in the thread as the better alternative to Insomnia, but it has a pricing page and commenters still say they expect any funded tool to monetise its way into the same behaviour; a hard 'no network, one-time price' stance is not its positioning.

competitors.name: Insomnia
competitors.gap: Commenters say it forces you to create a cloud account.

competitors.name: Postman
competitors.gap: The subject of the complaint: auto-installed AI plugins and data-sharing concerns, with users calling it enshittified.

ideas.title: SMS-Powered Expense Tracker
ideas.oneLiner: A Flutter expense tracker for India that builds your ledger from bank and UPI SMS alerts on-device, so you never type an expense.
ideas.problem: People keep abandoning expense trackers because of manual data entry, and bank-sync aggregators like Plaid and SimpleFin don't cover every bank or non-card spending. Commenters on a self-hosted expense tracker launch say reliable automatic data is the missing piece.
ideas.targetUsers: Salaried people and freelancers in India who pay mostly by UPI and cards and want automatic tracking without handing bank credentials to an aggregator.
ideas.monetization: Free for the last 3 months of history; ₹149/month or ₹999/year for unlimited history, export and budgets. Everything is processed on-device, which is the selling point.
mvp: Android SMS permission with on-device parsing of bank debit/credit and UPI messages into amount, merchant and date
Auto-categorisation by merchant with one-tap corrections that the app learns from
Cash and non-SMS entry in two taps (quick-add widget)
Monthly category view and a simple budget-per-category alert
CSV export and local encrypted backup

competitors.name: Plaid-based budgeting apps
competitors.gap: Per commenters, Plaid doesn't support all banks and has issues with various providers, and it doesn't capture spending not paid by cards.

competitors.name: SimpleFIN
competitors.gap: Used by the self-hosted tracker in the thread, which is limited to the banks SimpleFIN supports and to USD.

competitors.name: Spreadsheets
competitors.gap: The launch post's author calls his years of Excel tracking 'ugly and annoying to use'.

ideas.title: Clean Results Lens
ideas.oneLiner: A browser extension that hides AI-slop sites, fake fan wikis and paywalled links from Google results using a community-maintained blocklist.
ideas.problem: Searchers say result quality has dropped: fake wikis with inaccurate AI-written pages and SEO spam crowd out useful pages, and paywalled hits waste clicks. Commenters ask why search engines don't filter this themselves.
ideas.targetUsers: Heavy searchers, students, gamers looking up niche game info and researchers who currently scroll past junk results.
ideas.monetization: Free with a core blocklist; $3/month for auto-updating curated lists, per-topic lenses (games, recipes, health) and sync across browsers.
mvp: Content script that hides or dims results from domains on a blocklist on Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo
Crowd-sourced 'report this result as slop' button that feeds a shared list
Paywall badge and optional hiding for known paywalled domains
Personal allow/deny lists and an import of existing uBlacklist rules
Counter showing how many junk results were hidden

competitors.name: Kagi
competitors.gap: A paid search engine, so users must switch engines and pay a subscription; the commenters here are talking about filtering within the search they already use.

competitors.name: uBlacklist
competitors.gap: A manual block-list extension; users have to find and curate bad domains themselves and it has no slop or paywall detection.

ideas.title: Home Device Gatekeeper
ideas.oneLiner: A Raspberry Pi/OpenWrt appliance that blocks every new smart-home device by default and lets it reach only the domains it needs, from a crowd-sourced per-model allowlist.
ideas.problem: People are uneasy about how many connected devices in their homes phone home and what they send. Existing options are DNS blockers or MAC allowlists that give a device full outbound access once approved, and nobody maintains a per-model list of what a dishwasher or TV actually needs.
ideas.targetUsers: Privacy-minded home-lab users and smart-TV/appliance owners who can flash a router or run a Pi but don't want to hand-write firewall rules per device.
ideas.monetization: Open-source core; $5/month for the hosted, curated allowlist database and alerts, or a pre-flashed device sold at a margin.
mvp: Pi or OpenWrt image that puts new devices into a quarantine VLAN by default
Device fingerprinting by MAC vendor and DNS behaviour to suggest make/model
Per-device domain allowlist with a 'learn mode' that records what the device contacts over a week
Shared, upvoted allowlist profiles for popular TVs, fridges and appliances
Dashboard showing blocked connection attempts per device

competitors.name: Pi-hole / AdGuard Home
competitors.gap: Suggested in the thread, but they are DNS blocklists, not default-deny per device, and don't know which domains a given model needs to function.

competitors.name: GL.iNet allowlist mode
competitors.gap: A commenter says unknown MACs are denied until approved, but once unblocked a device gets unrestricted outbound access and there is no crowd-sourced list.

sources.title: Ask HN: uBlock Origin for the IoT devices in my house?
sources.quote: My dishwasher has a MAC address. So do dozens of other things in my house, and I have no idea what most of them send home.

sources.quote: Our Samsung fridge will mesh network with any Samsung TV specifically to exfiltrate marketing info, at least according to the manual.
